method: Real running app: window.app.engine.addLayer('object3d') (the same engine call the scene-tree "Add shape" action uses) creates a real standalone object3d leaf layer; window.app.ui.buildControls() renders the real Scene3DPanel docked Style tab (Vectura.UI.Scene3DPanel.build -> buildObjectPanel -> fillStyleControls). cases.reachedVia: Fill Style = Bundle . Count (survivor), then Bundle mode = Dithered

before.observed: Bundle . Count selected, Bundle mode = Integer pass count (default). No .vs3-lawnote.is-caveat present -- correct, bundleCount itself has no caveat.

after.crop: bundleDither-crop-native.png (native resolution, cropped to the caveat region + surrounding rows)
after.caveatText: A negative result, kept as one: waving the pass-count boundary made long-wave moire worse, not better, than the plain bundleCount baseline (3.43 vs 2.90 RMS on sphere·hatch), and R2 also dropped.
after.observed: LOOKED at bundleDither-crop-native.png: 'Fill Style' still reads 'Bundle . Count' (the survivor -- correct, the (i) popover stays on the survivor per the ruling), 'Bundle mode' reads 'Dithered', and the red caveat paragraph directly below it reads bundleDither's own measured caveat verbatim. Before this fix this line was empty (bundleCount.caveat is null).

cases.reachedVia: Fill Style = Continuous Field . Sigmoid (survivor), then Field floor = Ink-width floor

before.observed: Continuous Field . Sigmoid selected, Field metric = Screen metric, Field floor = Plot floor (both defaults). No .vs3-lawnote.is-caveat present -- correct, contFieldSigmoid itself has no caveat.

after.caveatText: It is a hatch-only law: on sphere·crosshatch it floods completely — R2, L* span, moire and highlight falloff all come back 0 because both families flood and the cell renders as a solid black disc with no tone left in it at all.
after.observed: LOOKED at contFieldTouch-crop-native.png: 'Field metric' reads 'Screen metric' (unchanged/default), 'Field floor' reads 'Ink-width floor', and the red caveat paragraph reads contFieldTouch's own measured caveat verbatim.
